sources.entry: Druid - Distributed, column-oriented, real-time analytics data store. (Source Code) Apache-2.0 Java/Docker

summary.one_liner: Apache Druid is a high-performance, real-time analytics database for fast queries and ingestion, positioned as an open source alternative to data warehouses.
summary.what_it_does: Druid is described as a real-time analytics database aimed at workflows needing fast queries and fast ingestion, such as powering UIs, ad-hoc operational queries, and high-concurrency workloads. It supports loading streaming and batch data through a point-and-click wizard in the built-in web console, which also shows datasources, segments, ingestion tasks, and services via SQL system tables. Users can prototype DruidSQL and native queries in a built-in query workbench. The README says Druid provides APIs over HTTP and JDBC for loading, managing, and querying data. Local and Docker quickstarts are mentioned, and the Kubernetes operator is maintained in a separate repository.
how_to_run: Get started with the local quickstart or the Docker quickstart (see the Druid documentation)
For Kubernetes, use the druid-operator, maintained in a separate repository
Build from source with JDK 25 (see the latest build guide)
To preview docs locally: install Node 22+, run npm|yarn install in the website directory, then npm|yarn start
notable: Web console with a point-and-click ingestion wizard and a query workbench for DruidSQL and native queries
Cluster management views backed by SQL system tables that expose the underlying query for each view
APIs over HTTP and JDBC for loading, managing, and querying data
Kubernetes operator maintained in a separate repository
caveats: Kubernetes deployment relies on a separate operator repository
Docs site local preview requires Node 22 or higher
